## SECTION 1.5. HISTORICAL BASE RATES

- **Turbine-OEM cyclicality base rate:** Power equipment margins are cyclical at the transactional layer — the sector's reference case (Siemens Energy, 2019–2021) showed multi-year losses before the current sold-out capacity cycle; GEV's own FY2022–FY2023 GAAP operating income was negative (–$2.88B, –$0.92B [Filed]) before turning positive in FY2024 (+$0.47B) and FY2025 (+$1.39B). Base-rate lesson: *do not extrapolate peak-cycle margins; do not extrapolate trough-cycle losses.* Our scenarios bracket both.
- **ROIC persistence:** FY2025 GAAP operating margin 3.6% [Arithmetic on filed] is a trough-to-ramp figure, not steady state; management's 20% adjusted EBITDA target "beyond 2028" [Estimate] implies a ~16pt margin migration — an aggressive but backlog-supported path. - **Backlog-to-revenue conversion base rate:** For capital-goods oligopolists, backlog/revenue > 3x historically converts with <5% slippage absent counterparty cancellations. GEV at 4.3x sits in the highest-visibility decile of its peer set [Assumption].
- **Model deviation justification:** We deviate from a single-archetype "cyclical machinery" multiple (which would imply ~10–12x FCF) because the installed-base annuity is a distinct, longer-duration asset; we value it as part of a blended duration DCF rather than clamping the exit multiple.
